caption: The login page
preconditions: Default DB authentication (no LDAP), so the 'Forgot password?' link shows
No SSO configured on the server (no SAML_PATH, no GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, OIDC_ENABLED false)
steps: Open #/workspace/monitoring and wait for [data-test-id="workspace-navigation"] to be visible
notes: Empty login form: Superdesk logo, 'username' and 'password' fields, 'Log In' button, 'Forgot password?' link (scripts/core/auth/login-modal.html). capture.mjs logs every context in before the first step, so the shot signs out first (avatar > Sign out). Sign out runs localStorage.clear() and reloads to the login page; the next shot's route load logs in again automatically ('session was logged out; logging in again'). Sign out stores LOGGED_OUT_LANGUAGE, so the login page shows in English for admin.

caption: Single sign-on buttons on the login page
preconditions: None on the server: the SSO buttons are switched on through TEST_APP_CONFIG (client-side only, the buttons are not clicked)
steps: Open #/workspace/monitoring and wait for [data-test-id="workspace-navigation"] to be visible

steps.script: localStorage.setItem('TEST_APP_CONFIG', JSON.stringify({saml_auth: true, saml_label: 'Single Sign On', google_auth: true})); location.reload();

steps: Wait for [data-test-id="login-page"] to show 'Log In with Google'
notes: Login form plus the 'or' divider and the two buttons 'Log In with Google' and 'Single Sign On' (the SAML button text is SAML_LABEL). The entry-level appConfig field cannot be used because Sign out clears localStorage, so the config is written after sign out and the page reloaded. init.ts merges TEST_APP_CONFIG over the server client_config, which is what turns the buttons on. capture.mjs logs every context in before the first step, so the shot signs out first (avatar > Sign out). Sign out runs localStorage.clear() and reloads to the login page; the next shot's route load logs in again automatically ('session was logged out; logging in again'). Sign out stores LOGGED_OUT_LANGUAGE, so the login page shows in English for admin.

caption: Asking for a password reset link
steps: Open #/workspace/monitoring and wait for [data-test-id="workspace-navigation"] to be visible
notes: Reset password page, step 1 (scripts/core/auth/reset-password.html): info text about the reset token, 'Email' field (leave empty), 'Get token' button, 'Have password? Sign in.' link. Do not click 'Get token'. Route after the click is #/reset-password/. capture.mjs logs every context in before the first step, so the shot signs out first (avatar > Sign out). Sign out runs localStorage.clear() and reloads to the login page; the next shot's route load logs in again automatically ('session was logged out; logging in again'). Sign out stores LOGGED_OUT_LANGUAGE, so the login page shows in English for admin.

caption: Logging in again after your session expired
preconditions: Admin is logged in (the capture context does this)
steps: Open #/workspace/monitoring and wait for [data-test-id="workspace-navigation"] to be visible
notes: Simulates an expired session: the session service watches localStorage 'sess:token'; removing it on the next digest (the click) shows the login screen with 'Your session has expired. Please log in again.' because the identity is still known (login-modal.html, p.session-error). If the overlay does not appear, delete the session on the server instead: evaluate fetch(localStorage.getItem('sess:href'), {method: 'DELETE', headers: {Authorization: localStorage.getItem('sess:token')}}) and then trigger any API call. The next shot's route load logs in again. Do not let dismissInterruptions log in before the shot is taken.
